description:
A concrete map construction loses the fact that its entry set is closed before
Map's Enumerable implementation invokes a reducer. The runtime result is
correct, but callback evidence widens each entry to `{any, any}`, creating
unnecessary reducer activations and dynamic arithmetic variants.

## Repro

    fn main() do
      dbg(Enum.reduce(%{:a => 1}, 0, fn ({_k, v}, acc) -> v + acc end))
    end

At origin/main `a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83`, interp,
JIT, and AOT all print `1`. `--dump activations` nevertheless reports:

    main/0#lambda@46-78/2[{any, any}, int]
      return: int | float
      callsites:
        @67-74 => Kernel.+/2(any, int) => int | float

    main/0#lambda@46-78/2[{any, any}, int | float]
      return: int | float
      callsites:
        @67-74 => Kernel.+/2(any, int | float) => int | float

The structurally equivalent list control:

    Enum.reduce([{:a, 1}], 0, fn ({_k, v}, acc) -> v + acc end)

has one reducer activation:

    main/0#lambda@45-77/2[{:a, int}, int]
      return: int
      callsites:
        @66-73 => Kernel.+/2(int, int) => int

The backend shows the first observable loss directly:

    Map.entry/2[%{:a => int}, int]
      return {any, any}

    Map.fz_map_entry_key/2[%{:a => int}, int]
      return any

    Map.fz_map_entry_value/2[%{:a => int}, int]
      return any

Consequently the Map program materializes `fz_op_add_ff`,
`fz_op_add_if`, and `fz_op_add_ii`; the list control needs only
`fz_op_add_ii`.

## Model constraint

The displayed input `%{:a => int}` is not an exact map type in the current
model. `MapSig` is an open record: it denotes any map containing at least the
listed fields. Map literals are inferred through that same `Types::map`
constructor.

It would therefore be unsound to derive `{:a, int}` from the existing Ty for
all callers: a value satisfying the open shape may contain additional entries
of unknown key and value types. The repair must preserve or introduce an
authoritative distinction between:

- a closed concrete map construction, whose complete entry set is known; and
- an open structural map constraint or unknown map, which must remain
  conservative.

The type system already exposes `map_known_keys` and `map_field_lookup`, but
those helpers alone do not prove closedness.

## Goal

Carry closed map-entry provenance across function and protocol boundaries and
derive the semantic element yielded by Map enumeration from that provenance.

For the one-entry literal above, `Map.entry/2` and the reducer must see
`{:a, int}`. For a closed multi-entry construction, preserve the known
key/value associations as entry alternatives rather than forming an unrelated
key/value Cartesian product. Open or unknown maps must continue to yield
`{any, any}` unless stronger evidence exists.

The runtime Map ABI may continue to return tagged `Any` words; this ticket is
about the semantic type and specialization evidence, not changing map
iteration or its C ABI.

## Strategy

1. Give closed map constructions a first-class semantic representation or
   equivalent provenance that survives calls and protocol dispatch. Do not
   reinterpret the existing open `MapSig` as exact.
2. Add one authoritative map-entry projection from that evidence.
3. Feed the projection into `Map.entry/2` and the Map Enumerable reducer
   callback boundary, allowing ordinary callback and contract propagation to
   carry the result.
4. Remove any superseded Map-entry fallback or duplicate derivation made
   unnecessary by the new authority.

Do not repair `Kernel.+/2`, hard-code this literal, or globally narrow arbitrary
maps.

## Checks

- The repro prints `1` on interp, JIT, and AOT.
- Its activation dump contains exactly the reducer input
  `[{:a, int}, int]`, returns `int`, and contains no `{any, any}` or recurrent
  `int | float` reducer activation.
- Its backend dump gives `Map.entry/2[%{:a => int}, int]` the semantic return
  `{:a, int}` and materializes only the integer arithmetic path required by the
  program.
- A closed heterogeneous-map test proves key/value associations remain
  correlated.
- An open-map control proves unmentioned entries are not narrowed
  unsoundly and still fall back to `{any, any}`.
- The list-of-tuples control remains unchanged.
- `map_enumerable` remains green on run, interp, and build.
- Full library and fixture matrix remain at baseline or better.

## Removed stale scope

`enum_take_drop_split` is no longer a sibling failure. At this baseline every
observed `Enum.take/2` call returns `[] | [int]`, including the Range source;
there is no `[any]` arm. Do not include it in this ticket's acceptance checks.
title: Preserve closed map-entry provenance through Enumerable so literal reducers do not receive {any, any}
